# Introduction to Amazon Bedrock

Amazon Bedrock is a fully managed service that offers foundation models from Amazon and leading AI companies through a single API.

<VideoSection youtubeId="f-rl_4Pd8dw" title="Bedrock overview" />

## What Bedrock gives you

- Unified API across model providers
- No infrastructure to manage
- Knowledge bases, agents, guardrails

```python
import boto3
client = boto3.client("bedrock-runtime")
response = client.invoke_model(modelId="anthropic.claude-3", body=payload)
```

<InfoCard title="Key idea">You pay per token — no GPU provisioning, no model hosting.</InfoCard>

## Quick check

<Quiz question="What does Bedrock manage for you?" options={["Your GPU clusters","Foundation model access via API","Your training data"]} answerIndex={1} explanation="Bedrock is a managed API over foundation models." />

> **Remember** — Bedrock ≠ training platform. It serves *inference + orchestration*.

items.author: nishant
items.md_content:
# AgentCore Runtime — Deploy & Invoke

The Runtime hosts your agent container and exposes a session-based invoke API.

## Deploy flow

1. Build container with your agent
2. `agentcore deploy` pushes to Runtime
3. Invoke with a session id — memory persists per session

<WarningCard title="Cold starts">First invoke can take 10-20s — warm with a ping for demos.</WarningCard>

<Quiz question="What keeps per-user conversation state?" options={["The container","Session id","The gateway"]} answerIndex={1} explanation="Runtime keys memory to the session id you pass." />

items.author: uday
items.md_content:
# Linux Foundations — Shell & Filesystem

Everything in Linux is a file — devices, processes, sockets.

## Core commands

```bash
ls -la
pwd
cd /var/log
cat syslog | tail -20
```

<TipCard title="Muscle memory">Learn `ls -lah` and `cd -` early — you'll use them hundreds of times a day.</TipCard>

1. pwd — where am I
2. ls — what is here
3. cd — go somewhere
4. cat / less — read files

<Quiz question="Which command shows the current directory?" options={["ls","pwd","cd","whoami"]} answerIndex={1} />

items.author: uday
items.md_content:
# Permissions & Users

`chmod`, `chown`, groups — the permission model in 20 minutes.

```bash
chmod 640 app.conf
chown app:ops app.conf
```

<Quiz question="What does chmod 640 give the group?" options={["read","write","execute"]} answerIndex={0} />

items.author: uday
items.md_content:
# Images & Containers

An image is a layered filesystem; a container is a running instance.

```bash
docker build -t app:v1 .
docker run -p 8080:80 app:v1
```

items.author: uday
items.md_content:
# Docker Compose Stacks

Multi-service apps in one YAML.

```yaml
services:
  web:
    image: app:v1
    ports: ["8080:80"]
  db:
    image: postgres:15
```

items.md_content:
# IAM — Accounts, Roles, Policies

Identity is the perimeter. Roles over keys, always.

<WarningCard title="Never">Long-lived access keys in code. Use roles / instance profiles.</WarningCard>

<Quiz question="Best practice for EC2 → S3 access?" options={["Access keys in env","IAM instance role","Hardcode in AMI"]} answerIndex={1} />

Object storage: STANDARD → INTELLIGENT → GLACIER.

```bash

aws s3 cp file.txt s3://my-bucket/
```
